title: IBM, Fermilab, and NVIDIA Unveil Modular Quantum Co-Design Platform, Slurm HRES Integration, and GPU QEC Tools at SC26 - Quantum Computing Report
gist: At SC26, IBM, NVIDIA and Fermilab announced a modular quantum-classical co-design platform co-locating DGX B200 systems with IBM Nighthawk QPUs; NVIDIA released CUDA-Q QEC 0.9.0 with the TCBP-JOBS GPU decoder; and Slurm 26.11 gained native multi-node QPU scheduling via QRMI/QDMI, adopted by IBM, Quantinuum, Pasqal, IQM, Alice & Bob and MQSC. The pieces show quantum hardware being absorbed into standard HPC stacks.

insights.claim: IBM, NVIDIA and Fermilab will physically co-locate NVIDIA DGX B200 systems with IBM Quantum Nighthawk processors in a modular quantum-classical co-design platform built on the IBM–Fermilab SQMS Center collaboration.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Both IBM and NVIDIA deepen DOE-lab entrenchment; NVIDIA rides quantum as GPU attach.
insights.locator: Fermilab, IBM, and NVIDIA Plan Modular Co-Design Platform

insights.claim: IBM's 120-qubit Nighthawk QPU deployed in the Fermilab co-design platform is specified at 7,500 two-qubit operations and 100k samples per second.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Benchmark spec for IBM's current flagship; compare against independent cloud benchmarks.

insights.claim: The Fermilab testbed's initial phase will emulate inter-module communication links to quantify how routing errors, latency and classical feedback affect multi-QPU execution, ahead of modular quantum scaling.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Modular/networked QPUs are the scaling path; interconnect latency is a key risk to track.

insights.claim: A later phase of the Fermilab co-design platform plans to integrate Fermilab's ultracoherent superconducting radio-frequency (SRF) cavities as quantum memories, entanglement buffers and bosonic error-correction resources.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hybrid cavity-plus-transmon architectures could become an alternative QEC route; watch for results.
insights.locator: A subsequent phase plans to integrate

insights.claim: Fermilab will coordinate access through HEPCloud for hybrid workflows studying lattice gauge theories, neutrino interactions and nuclear physics simulations.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Early quantum use cases at DOE labs are scientific simulation, not commercial workloads.

insights.claim: NVIDIA's TCBP-JOBS decoder, pairing Trajectory-Calibrated Belief Propagation with GPU-parallel Jittered Ordered Statistics Decoding Beam Search, delivers up to 4.5x lower logical error rate and 10x to 13,000x faster decoding than the Tesseract decoder.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is building a QEC software moat on GPUs, reinforcing CUDA lock-in into fault-tolerant quantum.

insights.claim: TCBP-JOBS maintains millisecond-scale serial latencies (4.08 ms for 12-round gross-code memory, 13.5 ms for logical lattice surgery at 0.2% error), suitable for neutral-atom and trapped-ion feed-forward but slower than superconducting cycle needs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: GPU decoders best fit slower modalities; superconducting players still need faster FPGA/ASIC decoders.
insights.locator: Detailed in a technical study by NVIDIA researchers

insights.claim: Exact search decoders such as Tesseract remain more accurate than NVIDIA's TCBP-JOBS in ultra-low-noise regimes of 0.01% to 0.05% physical error, so decoder choice depends on hardware noise level.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: As hardware improves, the advantage of GPU BP-style decoders may narrow — decoder market is not winner-take-all.
insights.locator: Detailed in a technical study by NVIDIA researchers

insights.claim: NVIDIA's CUDA-Q QEC 0.9.0 ships a containerized Decoding Server, composable parallel-window task graphs, and 1.3x to 3.2x faster Relay-BP kernels alongside TCBP-JOBS.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Productized QEC tooling makes NVIDIA the default decoding platform for many QPU makers.

insights.claim: Altera and Oxford Quantum Circuits demonstrated an NVQLink FPGA control bridge at SC26, part of a broader wave of GPU and FPGA QEC tooling.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: NVQLink is spreading to FPGA vendors, extending NVIDIA's quantum interconnect ecosystem.

themes.theme: Slurm makes QPUs schedulable HPC resources

insights.claim: NVIDIA, IBM and Pasqal integrated the open-source QRMI and QDMI interfaces into Slurm 26.11's Hierarchical Resources (HRES) scheduler, letting administrators allocate, reserve and account for QPUs alongside CPUs and GPUs under standard cluster policies.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Standardized scheduling lowers integration cost for HPC centers buying QPUs — expands the addressable on-prem quantum market.
insights.locator: Native Multi-Node QPU Scheduling in Slurm 26.11

insights.claim: Slurm 26.11 HRES treats QPUs as shared multi-node resources rather than node-local accelerators, which is why quantum hardware needed a hierarchical scheduler rather than GPU-style allocation.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Architectural signal: QPUs will be pooled facility assets, favoring vendors that integrate with HPC schedulers.
insights.quote: Because QPUs operate as shared multi-node resources rather than node-local accelerators
insights.locator: Native Multi-Node QPU Scheduling in Slurm 26.11

insights.claim: Roughly 30 supercomputing centers worldwide are deploying more than 50 quantum processors, a fleet the Slurm 26.11 QPU integration aims to serve without custom middleware.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Sizing datapoint for the on-prem HPC-integrated quantum market.
insights.locator: Native Multi-Node QPU Scheduling in Slurm 26.11

insights.claim: Slurm 26.11 HRES quantum scheduling has been adopted by IBM, Quantinuum, Pasqal, IQM, Alice & Bob and MQSC.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Broad cross-modality adoption signals Slurm becoming the de facto quantum-HPC integration standard.
